text:
mina: Hi all, first-week question: I'm demoing a prototype tomorrow and using a hosted API key from the office wifi. I'm intermittently getting 429s and once got a truncated stream. Who's the fastest person to ask for a small hosted quota bump or a sandbox key for the demo? Also, does IT need anything special whitelisted on the proxy?
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood, Mina! :tada: For demo bumps DM devops or post the demo window here. See the onboarding checklist: https://redwood.dev/onboarding
devops: Hi @mina  we can provision a 24-72h hosted bump or a sandbox key (sandbox has separate quota). For hosted bumps include the demo time window, model (e.g., rwd-1-small), and expected peak requests per second. Sandbox is usually fastest for same-day.
it-team: Two quick things for IT: 1) Allow outbound to api.redwood.ai and our published egress CIDR (link on internal infra page). 2) Exempt streaming endpoints from buffering/proxy re-chunking so Transfer-Encoding: chunked isn't stripped. Many corporate proxies terminate TLS and buffer responses which can truncate streams.
mina: here's the curl I ran (sanitized token):
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' -N -v
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_zz99yy88
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
(no retry-after)
Also saw `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` occasionally during streaming.
infra: If the same key works off your phone hotspot but fails on office Wi-Fi, that's almost certainly an IP NAT bucket issue. Many users behind a corporate NAT share one egress IP and can hit IP-level rate limits.
sam: Helpful debug steps: 1) try tethering to hotspot to see if 429s go away 2) paste `x-request-id` if you hit 429s so we can trace the gateway logs 3) check client concurrency and batching. For embeddings/chat, batching and reducing parallel connections can help a lot.
security: Reminder: hosted API tokens are bearer tokens (no interactive MFA for API calls). Do not paste keys in public channels; store them in Vault/Secrets Manager. For demos we prefer sandbox keys or Vault-issued ephemeral creds.
devops: Quick workaround options: 
- Issue a sandbox key (separate quota) immediately via DM.
- Issue a short hosted bump if you need the hosted environment for demo fidelity (takes a bit longer).
- We can create ephemeral creds via Vault for the session.
mina: Demo is tomorrow 10:00-10:30 PST, expect ~10 req/s peak, mostly streaming chat. Sandbox sounds fine if protocol is identical.
it-team: Protocols are identical. If you must use hosted, give devops the demo window and we can ask IT to whitelist the egress CIDR and ensure the proxy doesn't coalesce/chunk responses. Also check MTU if you see resets consistently.
sam: If you still want hosted bump, include model, expected token units, and demo window in the request. If you hit 429s again paste `x-request-id` and we'll lookup traces. Also try curl with `--http1.1 -N` to avoid proxy HTTP/2 buffering during tests.
ops-bot: Please redact keys and use placeholders when pasting logs.
mina: Thanks everyone, I'll DM devops for a sandbox key and run a hotspot test to confirm. Appreciate the pointers! :thumbsup:
